newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-PANIS HAS SECOND LEG OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PANIS HAS SECOND LEG OPERATION.

text.p: French Formula One driver Olivier Panis, who broke both his legs in a crash at Sunday's Canadian Grand Prix, had a second operation on his right leg Tuesday and was recovering well, a hospital spokeswoman said.
The second surgery, which took 45 minutes, was not considered major, a Sacre-Coeur hospital spokeswoman said.
Panis, who underwent four hours of surgery on Sunday to repair both fractured legs, has had the broken bones stabilised with screws to avoid the need for casts and favour a speedy recovery.
Doctors have been careful not to speculate about how soon Panis, 30, would resume driving for the Prost-Mugen Honda team. They said most people require between two and four months to fully recover.

Panis, who was enjoying a banner season, slammed hard into a tire barrier on the 53rd lap. The accident occurred as the back end of his car came loose and he lost control coming around a curve on the back side of the course.
The car hit an inside retaining wall before slamming into the tire barrier -- scattering tires all over the track.
The debris forced the race to be ended after 54 of 69 scheduled laps, and Germany's Michael Schumacher was declared the winner.
Panis, who drives for Formula One racing legend Alain Prost, won last year's prestigious Monaco Grand Prix.
